editions.title: CR7 Edition
editions.headline: The First Man to Score at Five World Cups: *Cristiano Ronaldo*
editions.subheadline: Six World Cups, from Germany 2006 to North America 2026, in one framed shadow box with gold foil accents. Arrives ready to hang.
editions.story: From his first World Cup in Germany in 2006 to becoming the first man to score at five World Cups in Qatar 2022, every chapter of Cristiano Ronaldo’s international journey sits in order inside one frame.

cards.label: DEBUT
cards.description: His first World Cup. He scored against Iran in Frankfurt as Portugal reached their first semi-final in 40 years.

cards.label: CAPTAIN
cards.description: His first World Cup as Portugal captain.

cards.label: BALLON D’OR
cards.description: Arrived as the reigning Ballon d’Or winner, set up a late equaliser against the USA in Manaus and scored the winner against Ghana in Brasília.

cards.label: SOCHI HAT-TRICK
cards.description: Scored a hat-trick against Spain in Sochi, finishing with a late free kick to make it 3–3.

cards.label: FIVE WORLD CUPS
cards.description: Scored against Ghana to become the first man to score at five World Cups.

cards.label: SIXTH WORLD CUP
cards.description: The 2026 World Cup, hosted across the USA, Canada and Mexico.

editions.title: Lionel Messi Edition
editions.headline: Sixteen Years Chasing It, One Night in Lusail to Lift It: *Messi*
editions.subheadline: Six World Cups, from his debut in Germany 2006 to North America 2026, in one framed shadow box with gold foil accents.
editions.quote: "From an 18-year-old debut to lifting the trophy in Lusail."
editions.story: From his first World Cup goal at 18 in Germany to two Golden Balls and Argentina’s third star in Qatar, every chapter of Lionel Messi’s World Cup journey sits in order inside one frame.

cards.label: DEBUT
cards.description: His first World Cup. At 18 he scored against Serbia and Montenegro, becoming Argentina’s youngest World Cup scorer.

cards.label: NO. 10
cards.description: His first World Cup in Argentina’s No. 10 shirt.

cards.label: GOLDEN BALL
cards.description: Led Argentina to the final at the Maracanã and won the tournament’s Golden Ball.

cards.label: ST PETERSBURG
cards.description: Scored against Nigeria in St Petersburg to help send Argentina through to the knockout stage.

cards.label: WORLD CHAMPION
cards.description: Scored twice in the final, won the World Cup with Argentina and collected a second Golden Ball.

cards.label: SIXTH WORLD CUP
cards.description: The 2026 World Cup, hosted across the USA, Canada and Mexico.

editions.title: Neymar Jr Edition
editions.headline: The Goal in Qatar That Matched Pelé’s Record: *Neymar Jr*
editions.subheadline: From Brazil 2014 to North America 2026, four World Cups in one framed shadow box with gold foil accents.
editions.story: From carrying a host nation’s hopes at Brazil 2014 to equalling Pelé’s Brazil scoring record in Qatar, all four of Neymar Jr’s World Cups sit in order inside one frame.

cards.label: HOST NATION
cards.description: His first World Cup, at home. He scored twice in the opening match against Croatia in São Paulo and twice more against Cameroon in Brasília.

cards.label: SAMARA
cards.description: Scored and set up a goal against Mexico in Samara to take Brazil into the quarter-finals.

cards.label: PELÉ’S RECORD
cards.description: Scored in extra time against Croatia to equal Pelé’s record of 77 goals for Brazil.

cards.label: LAST DANCE
cards.description: The 2026 World Cup, hosted across the USA, Canada and Mexico.

editions.title: Zinedine Zidane Edition
editions.headline: Two Headers in Paris, a Golden Ball in Berlin: *Zidane*
editions.subheadline: Three World Cups, from France 1998 to Germany 2006, in one framed shadow box with gold foil accents.
editions.story: From two headers in the 1998 final in Paris to the Golden Ball in Germany 2006, every chapter of Zinedine Zidane’s World Cup journey sits in order inside one frame.

cards.label: WORLD CHAMPION
cards.description: Scored twice in the final against Brazil as France won the World Cup on home soil.

cards.label: DEFENDING CHAMPION
cards.description: France arrived as defending champions; Zidane, carrying an injury, played in the final group match.

cards.label: GOLDEN BALL
cards.description: Led France to the final in Berlin, scored in it, and won the tournament’s Golden Ball.

editions.title: Diego Maradona Edition
editions.headline: Mexico ’86, the Goal of the Century and the Cup: *Maradona*
editions.subheadline: Four World Cups, from Spain 1982 to USA 1994, in one framed shadow box with gold foil accents.
editions.story: From his World Cup debut in Spain 1982 to lifting the trophy in Mexico City in 1986, every chapter of Diego Maradona’s World Cup journey sits in order inside one frame.

cards.label: FIRST WORLD CUP
cards.description: His first World Cup, at 21. He scored twice against Hungary before Argentina went out in the second group stage.

cards.label: WORLD CHAMPION
cards.description: Captained Argentina to the title, scored the Goal of the Century against England and won the Golden Ball.

cards.label: RUNNER-UP
cards.description: Led the defending champions back to the final in Rome, where they lost to West Germany.

cards.label: FOURTH WORLD CUP
cards.description: His fourth World Cup. His goal against Greece was the last of his 34 for Argentina.

editions.title: Toni Kroos Edition
editions.headline: Two Goals in the 7–1, Then the Trophy in Rio: *Toni Kroos*
editions.subheadline: Three World Cups, from South Africa 2010 to Russia 2018, in one framed shadow box with gold foil accents.
editions.story: From his World Cup debut at 20 in South Africa to lifting the trophy in Rio in 2014, every chapter of Toni Kroos’s World Cup journey sits in order inside one frame.

cards.label: FIRST WORLD CUP
cards.description: His first World Cup, at 20. Germany finished third in South Africa.

cards.label: WORLD CHAMPION
cards.description: Scored twice in the 7–1 semi-final against Brazil and won the World Cup in Rio.

cards.label: LAST-GASP WINNER
cards.description: Scored a last-minute free kick to beat Sweden; Germany went out in the group stage.

editions.title: Sergio Ramos Edition
editions.headline: Four World Cups, One Star on His Chest: *Sergio Ramos*
editions.subheadline: Four World Cups, from Germany 2006 to Russia 2018, in one framed shadow box with gold foil accents.
editions.story: From his World Cup debut at 20 in Germany to winning it all in South Africa and captaining Spain in Russia, every chapter of Sergio Ramos’s World Cup journey sits in order inside one frame.

cards.label: FIRST WORLD CUP
cards.description: His first World Cup, at 20, at right-back for Spain.

cards.label: WORLD CHAMPION
cards.description: Played every minute as Spain won their first World Cup.

cards.label: DEFENDING CHAMPION
cards.description: Spain went out in the group stage as defending champions.

cards.label: CAPTAIN
cards.description: Captained Spain at his fourth World Cup.

editions.title: Luka Modrić Edition
editions.headline: The Maestro Who Took Croatia to a World Cup Final: *Modrić*
editions.subheadline: Four chapters of a legendary career, 2012 to 2022, in one framed shadow box with gold foil accents.
editions.story: From joining Real Madrid in 2012 to leading Croatia to the World Cup final and the Ballon d’Or, every chapter of Luka Modrić’s career sits in order inside one frame.

cards.label: THE ARRIVAL
cards.description: Joined Real Madrid from Tottenham in 2012.

cards.label: LA DÉCIMA
cards.description: Won Real Madrid’s tenth European Cup.

cards.label: BALLON D’OR
cards.description: Led Croatia to the World Cup final, won the Golden Ball and then the Ballon d’Or.

cards.label: THIRD PLACE
cards.description: Captained Croatia to third place at the World Cup in Qatar.

editions.title: Raúl González Edition
editions.headline: The Angel of Madrid and Three European Cups: *Raúl*
editions.subheadline: Four chapters of a legendary career, 1994 to 2002, in one framed shadow box with gold foil accents.
editions.story: From his Real Madrid debut at 17 to three European Cups in five years, every chapter of Raúl González’s Madrid story sits in order inside one frame.

cards.label: PRODIGY
cards.description: Made his Real Madrid debut at 17 in 1994 and quickly became a regular.

cards.label: LA SÉPTIMA
cards.description: Won Real Madrid’s seventh European Cup.

cards.label: CHAMPIONS
cards.description: Scored in the final as Real Madrid beat Valencia.

cards.label: LA NOVENA
cards.description: Won Real Madrid’s ninth European Cup.

editions.title: Ángel Di María Edition
editions.headline: Goals in an Olympic, a Copa América and a World Cup Final: *Di María*
editions.subheadline: Four chapters of a legendary career, 2008 to 2022, in one framed shadow box with gold foil accents.
editions.story: From the Olympic final in Beijing to scoring in the World Cup final in Qatar, every chapter of Ángel Di María’s career sits in order inside one frame.

cards.label: OLYMPIC GOLD
cards.description: Scored the winning goal in the Olympic final.

cards.label: LA DÉCIMA
cards.description: Named man of the match as Real Madrid won its tenth European Cup.

cards.label: COPA AMÉRICA
cards.description: Scored the only goal of the Copa América final against Brazil.

cards.label: WORLD CHAMPION
cards.description: Scored in the World Cup final as Argentina became champions.

editions.title: Karim Benzema Edition
editions.headline: From the 2010 Sticker Album to the 2022 Ballon d’Or: *Benzema*
editions.subheadline: Three World Cup stickers, from South Africa 2010 to Qatar 2022, in one framed shadow box with gold foil accents.
editions.story: From the 2010 sticker album to arriving in Qatar as the reigning Ballon d’Or winner, Karim Benzema’s World Cup story with France sits in order inside one frame.

cards.label: THE STICKER
cards.description: In the 2010 sticker album, but left out of France’s final squad for South Africa.

cards.label: THREE GOALS
cards.description: Scored three goals as France reached the quarter-finals in Brazil.

cards.label: BALLON D’OR
cards.description: Named in the squad as the reigning Ballon d’Or winner, but a thigh injury ruled him out on the eve of the tournament.
